title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Shared borrow-driven radix-4 combinational divider
motivation:
The only recorded bench result has a 199.837 ns worst path with 156
cells through forwarding and the combinational ALU, and median Fmax
is only 5.442 MHz. The ALU expresses signed and unsigned division and
remainder separately with / and %, exposing a large, deeply cascaded
arithmetic network to Gowin synthesis. Shortening this network can
improve every CoreMark cycle even when that cycle does not divide.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace just the real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU implementation in alu.sv with
one shared, fully combinational radix-4 restoring divider. It produces
quotient and remainder together in 16 unrolled steps, each consuming
two dividend bits. Precompute exact unsigned 34-bit divisor multiples
D, 2D, and 3D. At each step compute trial-minus-multiple for all three
candidates in parallel; use the subtraction borrow and a priority
select to choose the largest nonnegative candidate and its two-bit
quotient digit. Do not put a separate comparator before a subtractor.
Exploit the statically bounded partial-dividend width: step j needs
W=2*(j+1) remainder bits, a W+1-bit difference, and a check that the
chosen 34-bit divisor multiple has no set bits at positions W and
higher; explicitly zero-extend both W-bit subtraction operands. This avoids
needless full-width arithmetic at the early steps without truncating
overflowing multiples or accepting an invalid subtraction.

Normalize operands to unsigned magnitudes only for signed DIV/REM,
then restore quotient sign with a[31] XOR b[31] and remainder sign
with a[31]. Explicitly preserve division-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1
results, and keep all RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS substitutions unchanged.
This is a local combinational arithmetic optimization: retain the
multiplier, other ALU operations, ALU ports, pipeline stages,
retirement contract, and bus handshake behavior. The proposed gain
comes from halving the serial quotient-selection steps and sharing
the four division operations, with unchanged iterations per cycle.

title: Remove combinational division from EX with a shared iterative divider
motivation:
The baseline reaches only 5.442 MHz and its worst Gowin path spans 156
cells through forwarding, EX and the ALU. The ALU currently implements
signed and unsigned division and remainder as combinational / and %
operators. These unrolled arithmetic networks impose their delay and
routing cost on the whole processor, including cycles executing ordinary
integer instructions. There are no recorded structural attempts or
LESSONS.md entries for this fixture. Replacing the divider's spatially
unrolled datapath with a sequential unit is the strongest structural
opportunity suggested by the available timing and RTL evidence.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the single-retirement in-order pipeline and existing combinational
integer ALU and multiplier, but move DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU into one
clocked radix-2 restoring divider. Use a registered 32-bit divisor,
dividend/quotient shift register and 33-bit partial remainder; perform
one compare/subtract-and-select step per cycle for 32 iterations.
Register signed magnitude preparation and final quotient/remainder sign
correction separately so no cycle chains normalization, iteration and
correction. Sharing quotient and remainder computation eliminates all
real combinational / and % hardware from the reachable production ALU.
Handle divisor zero and signed INT_MIN/-1 with explicit RV32M results.

Accept a divide only when ID/EX contains a valid divide instruction and
the older MEM transaction is not blocking EX/MEM. Snapshot the actual
forwarded source values, operation and instruction metadata on acceptance.
Hold PC and ID/EX while the divider owns EX, but allow older EX/MEM and
MEM/WB instructions to drain. When memory is ready, EX/MEM receives a
cleared bubble while the divide is incomplete; when memory is stalled,
retain its outstanding request using the existing dmem hold behavior.
A completed divide holds its result until EX/MEM can accept it exactly
once. Then release the frontend, forward the registered result using
the existing EX/MEM and MEM/WB paths, and retire through channel 0 with
the original forwarded operands and PC information. Reset cancels all
divider state. Never repeat requests, divide launches or retirements.

Preserve the exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas as a single-cycle bypass
in formal builds so the 32-step divider does not exceed the existing
bounded formal budget. Real simulation and FPGA builds must use the
iterative arithmetic. Keep every existing DIV/REM arithmetic expectation
in test_alu.py, adapting its helper to the ALU's new divider handshake,
and add core-level stall and dependency coverage. Decoder legality,
alignment traps, nret=1 IO and all evaluation
contracts remain intact. The predicted fitness gain comes from a much
shorter clock period across all instructions; added division cycles are
the principal risk and must be measured with bracketed CoreMark under
the existing random instruction and data stalls.

title: Small bimodal next-PC predictor eliminates taken-branch bubbles
motivation:
The baseline fetch payload is combinational, with no IF/ID register, so
every taken branch or jump resolved in EX discards one younger instruction
and costs one bubble. CoreMark repeatedly executes loop and decision
branches, making direction prediction a direct way to reduce measured
cycles. The reported 199.837 ns critical path passes through the existing
combinational M-extension ALU; a small predictor can improve iterations
per cycle without attempting an unrelated arithmetic redesign. There are
no recorded predictor attempts or distilled lessons for this fixture.

Reference replay of the canonical compiled 2K, -O3, 10-iteration CoreMark
workload finds 529,588 conditional branches at 158 distinct PCs, with
294,425 taken branches, 49,367 JALs and 13,735 JALRs between the markers.
This 64-entry hashed table incurs 41,559 direction misses (92.15% accuracy),
versus 111,175 for static backward-taken/forward-not-taken prediction.
These measurements support a small adaptive predictor rather than a
larger target table or static direction alone.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one lightweight fetch-time next-PC predictor: a 64-entry untagged
bimodal table of two-bit saturating conditional-branch counters, indexed
by PC[7:2] XOR PC[13:8], plus a valid bit per entry. Cold entries use
backward-taken/forward-not-taken direction until the first EX resolution
initializes the counter to weakly taken or weakly not taken. On subsequent
resolutions increment or decrement with saturation. Predecode only legal
BRANCH funct3 values and JAL from the raw fetched instruction, construct
their B/J immediate, and use one PC-relative target adder. Predict an
aligned conditional target when its direction is taken, and an aligned
JAL target unconditionally. All other instructions, including JALR,
predict PC+4. No BTB, return stack, cache, or pipeline-depth change.

Carry the full predicted next PC with each accepted instruction through
IF and ID/EX. Compute the architectural next PC in EX using the existing
forwarded operands, branch conditions, JAL/JALR targets and misalignment
trap behavior. Redirect and flush only when a valid instruction can
advance out of EX and its resolved next PC differs from the prediction;
the recovery target is the resolved next PC, including PC+4 for a falsely
predicted taken branch or a trapped target. Correctly predicted taken
branches and JALs retain the younger target instruction without a bubble.
RVFI pc_wdata always uses the architectural resolution, never speculation.

Compute predictions from raw imem_data independently of stall/flush
outputs, so the load-use hazard path cannot form a combinational loop.
Advance the PC along a prediction only when fetch is actually accepted:
no instruction-bus stall, load-use bubble, data-bus hold, or recovery.
Reset has highest priority; an EX recovery overrides an instruction-bus
stall; otherwise the PC holds on stalled acceptance. Suppress recovery
and predictor updates while EX is held by data-memory backpressure;
re-evaluate and update exactly once when that valid EX instruction
advances. Only legal, valid, nontrapping conditional branches train the
table. Reset clears predictor validity, and bubbles never train it.

Keep the single-channel nret=1 IO and all existing illegal-instruction,
trap, forwarding, memory, retirement-order, and CoreMark checks intact.
A control-flow cycle model using the reference instruction stream and
the fixture's exact xorshift32 bus sequence reproduces the baseline's
4,491,485 marker-bracketed cycles exactly. Modeling simultaneous fetch
prediction and EX training, the load-use logic, one-shot recovery and
data-memory holds predicts 4,190,281 cycles for this design: 7.19% higher
throughput at unchanged Fmax. This is cycle-model evidence; implemented
RTL correctness and FPGA timing still need the existing gates. Expect
about 7% fitness gain, with approximately 2.4% Fmax-loss headroom before
falling below the 4.6% acceptance margin. Direction aliasing and routing
cost are the main uncertainties. Validate with directed pipeline
tests, existing formal and cosim gates, and stalled CoreMark CRCs; assess
the actual gain using the existing marker-bracketed cycle count and
median Gowin Fmax, requiring more than 4.6% fitness improvement.

title: Remove redirect feedback from decode data with control-only bubbles
motivation:
The champion reaches 46.833 MHz after removing combinational division.
Its reported worst path now traverses ID, EX, IF, hazard control and ID
again, ending at an ID/EX operand register. The frontend currently turns
every redirect or unavailable fetch into a NOP instruction, feeding
late EX branch resolution back through instruction selection, register
addresses, decoding and register reads. ID also clears its entire wide
payload on flush. These bubble implementations expose decode data to
the late redirect signal although only validity and side-effect control
need to change. The earlier micro_opt attempt optimized the obsolete
combinational divider and achieved only 3.55%; this proposal instead
targets the champion's measured control-feedback bottleneck.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Represent frontend bubbles by invalid validity and zero side-effect
control, rather than by selecting a NOP and clearing every data bit.
In IF, pass the raw imem instruction and current PC through regardless
of flush, and let flush/redirect affect only out.valid and the existing
prioritized PC update. In ID, keep reset behavior, but capture or hold
the operand, immediate, PC, instruction and register-address payload
using only the existing stall enable, independently of flush. Update
valid and the control bundle separately: reset or flush clears both;
otherwise an unstalled invalid fetch captures valid=0 and ctrl='0;
an unstalled valid fetch captures the normal validated decoder control.
A flush must still invalidate controls even when stall is asserted,
preserving the existing reset/flush-over-stall priority. Arbitrary
payload in bubbles must never enable forwarding, redirects, divider
requests, memory transactions, writes or retirement.

Replace the NOP's accidental hazard suppression with an explicit
qualification of load-use detection by io_imemReady. Use raw
instruction register fields for the comparison, and qualify the load
in ID/EX with its valid bit. Do not use redirect, flush_if or if_id.valid
in the load-use comparison or payload stall enable: that would restore
the feedback path being removed. A legal load cannot simultaneously
redirect, and invalid ID/EX controls are zero, so redirect suppression
is unnecessary for this comparator. Preserve
every real load-use bubble, dmem hold, divide wait, MEM/WB retained
forwarding value and redirect-over-fetch-stall rule. Do not change
source-use decoding or the architectural pipeline's cycle schedule.
Preserve the current nret=1 ports, ALTOPS substitutions, iterative
divider and all illegal and misalignment trap behavior.

This local bubble-control optimization should remove the EX-to-IF-to-ID
data feedback and wide flush fanout without adding any stage or changing
accepted instructions. The expected gain is higher median Gowin Fmax
at the same marker-bracketed CoreMark cycle count. Require the unchanged
formal, arithmetic and cosim gates, canonical CoreMark CRCs and measured
fitness more than 4.6% above 104.26; the main uncertainty is which path
becomes critical after the redirect/decode feedback is removed.

title: Separate pipeline payload storage from bubble and redirect control
motivation:
The accepted iterative-divider hypothesis raised fitness to 104.26 with
median Gowin Fmax 46.833 MHz and 4,491,817 bracketed CoreMark cycles.
Its reported worst path is now 25.737 ns across 32 cells, from the
register file to ID/EX operand storage through ID, EX, IF and hazard
control. In the current topology, EX redirect replaces the fetched
instruction with a NOP before register-file addressing and load-use
comparisons, and the resulting flush/hold controls reset or enable the
entire ID/EX payload. This creates a long feedback path through data
selection and high-fanout control. No prior attempt has separated
payload movement from instruction validity; LESSONS.md is absent.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the existing frontend around independently clocked payload
and valid state, keeping the same pipeline depth and retirement width.
Fetch must present raw imem_data and its PC to decode even on a redirect
or instruction-bus stall; represent an unavailable or killed instruction
by validity, rather than replacing its 32-bit encoding with a NOP.
Decode, register-file addresses, immediates and raw dependency comparisons
must consequently have no combinational dependence on EX redirect.

In ID/EX, retain payload only for genuine downstream ownership: an older
data-memory stall or an active/incomplete divide. Otherwise capture the
decoded payload and operands, even when a load-use bubble, redirect or
missing fetch makes that capture invalid. Reset and flush update the
valid state separately. A load-use hazard holds the PC and clears next
ID/EX validity for one cycle while the load advances; redirect clears
next validity and redirects the PC in the existing resolution cycle.
Neither event should clear, zero-mux or control the clock enable of the
wide operand, immediate, PC and instruction registers. Gate load-use
detection by valid EX and fetched instructions, with the original raw
source-field comparisons for accepted fetches. Keep reset initialization
compatible with the existing checks; removing architectural register-file
reset is outside this proposal.

Make validity authoritative before downstream effects: an invalid ID/EX
payload cannot redirect, launch division, advertise a producing rd, issue
a memory request or retire. Clear EX/MEM reg_write, mem_read and mem_write
flags for invalid captures before their forwarding/memory consumers; do not
reintroduce flush-controlled wide payload muxes. Keep an outstanding
EX/MEM request stable through dmem backpressure. Preserve MEM/WB's
existing retained forwarding data on a stall even after its retirement
valid is cleared: bypass availability and retirement validity have
different lifetimes, so blindly gating that bypass with rvfi_valid would
be incorrect. Preserve the divider's operand snapshot, exactly-once
result consumption, real RV32M arithmetic and ALTOPS behavior.

Preserve the champion's instruction acceptance and branch recovery
cycles, including its PC redirect priority and backend hold semantics.
This is one structural change to the pipeline's control/data topology,

title: PC-indexed next-PC predictor with timing-isolated recovery
motivation:
The current champion reaches 104.26 iter/sec using the shared iterative
divider. Its worst Gowin path is now 25.737 ns through ID, EX, IF,
hazard logic and back into ID, rather than through division. The prior
predictor attempt hyp-20261004-003-r1s2 reduced marker-bracketed CoreMark
cycles from roughly 4.491 million to 4.190 million, but was evaluated
on the older combinational-divider parent and reached only 5.347 MHz.
That result supports prediction's cycle benefit, not a timing result
for prediction on the current champion. No LESSONS.md is present.
A predictor that reads only the registered fetch PC and whose recovery
does not mask the instruction before decoding can remove taken-control
bubbles without lengthening the champion's redirect feedback path.
Reference replay of the canonical 2K, -O3, 10-iteration workload sees
529,588 conditional branches, 49,367 JALs and 13,735 JALRs between the
markers. A 32-entry tagged predictor incurs 73,619 next-PC misses,
versus 357,527 taken-control redirects without prediction. A 64-entry
version saves only another 11,068 misses while doubling table storage.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Starting from the CURRENT iterative-divider champion, implement one
compact fetch-time next-PC predictor: a 32-entry direct-mapped tagged
branch target buffer indexed by PC[6:2]. Each entry holds a valid bit,
the full PC[31:7] tag, the target's 30 aligned upper bits, a
conditional-versus-unconditional bit, and a two-bit saturating direction
counter. A matching unconditional entry predicts its target; a matching
conditional entry predicts its target only when the counter is taken.
A miss predicts PC+4. Learn legal conditional branches, JAL and JALR at
EX completion, using the resolved indirect target for JALR. Initialize
a new conditional entry weakly toward its actual outcome; subsequently
saturate its counter and update its PC-relative target even on not-taken
outcomes. Jumps are always taken entries. Read the table directly from
the PC, independently of imem_data, decode, flush and hazard signals.
Require a computed target with both low bits zero before installing or
training an entry, including a not-taken branch's immediate target.
Keep target/tag storage unreset with resettable validity, allowing
compact asynchronous-read, synchronous-write distributed-memory
inference; no BRAM read latency or new fetch pipeline stage is required.

Carry the selected predicted next PC through IF and ID/EX. Advance the
fetch PC along it only when the instruction is accepted, with reset
first, advancing EX recovery next, and frontend hold otherwise. EX
computes the same architectural next PC, link value and alignment trap
as today. Recovery means a valid, actually advancing EX instruction's
resolved next PC differs from its carried prediction. Redirect to the
architectural next PC, including PC+4 for a falsely predicted taken
branch or trapped target. Correct predictions retain the younger
instruction. RVFI pc_wdata always reports architectural resolution.
Factor conditional recovery so comparison of the carried prediction
against target and PC+4 occurs in parallel with the branch comparator;
the late branch outcome selects between one-bit mismatch results,
rather than preceding a wide next-PC mux and equality reduction.
Train exactly once per advancing legal nontrapping control instruction;
do not train during dmem holds, division waits, reset or invalid bubbles.
Full tags and target comparison make collisions and stale JALR targets
performance events with normal recovery, never correctness assumptions.

Make recovery timing part of this predictor integration. Stop using EX
recovery to replace raw imem_data with a NOP before the load-use
comparisons and decoder. Fetch validity describes bus availability;
recovery independently kills the younger ID/EX validity. Compute
load-use from the raw instruction, with no recovery-to-instruction-data
path. For a recovery or load-use bubble, invalidate ID/EX while keeping
the operand/control payload capture or hold decisions independent of
recovery; do not use the late branch result as a select on every ID/EX
payload bit. Every side effect of an invalid instruction must be gated:
no EX redirect, divider launch, predictor update, EX/MEM forwarding
producer, register write or memory request. Emit inert EX/MEM control for invalid
ID/EX payloads. Preserve flush priority for validity and preserve the
older dmem request, retained MEM/WB forwarding and held divide snapshot.
Qualify ID/EX load-use detection with validity so a bubble retaining an
old load payload cannot repeatedly stall fetch. Keep the existing
retained MEM/WB forwarding source usable even after a dmem hold clears
its retirement validity; this older data is distinct from squashed EX.
This removes the reported EX-to-IF-to-hazard-to-ID operand feedback while
retaining immediate misprediction correction and existing stage count.

Suppress EX recovery while an older dmem operation holds EX, and recover
when that instruction really advances. Recovery must override imem
unavailability and squash the younger instruction on that edge. Holds
preserve the instruction's original prediction, not a later table read.
Reset clears predictor validity. Keep the existing radix-2 divider,
actual RV32M results and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS behavior unchanged; preserve
nret=1 ports, trap discipline, retirement order and all evaluation gates.

The expected gain combines fewer taken-control bubbles with removal of
the champion's late redirect feedback through instruction masking.
A pipeline cycle model uses the reference instruction stream, the exact
two-draw xorshift32 bus sequence, load-use logic, simultaneous fetch
lookup and EX training, one-shot recovery, dmem holds and divider waits.

champion's 4,491,817 cycles exactly. It predicts 4,208,611 cycles for

throughput gain for twice the target/tag storage. Prefer the smaller
table to limit lookup and routing costs. This is cycle-model evidence,

roughly 5% Fmax improvement from recovery isolation; neither that
timing gain nor correctness is proven until implementation. There is
approximately 2% Fmax-loss headroom before the modeled cycle gain falls
below the acceptance margin. Target/tag lookup routing is the main risk.

median Fmax times bracketed iterations/cycle exceeds 104.26 by 4.6%.

title: Fold forwarding and ALU source selection into one operand mux
motivation:
The champion scores 119.64 iter/sec at 53.739 MHz. After the iterative
divider and payload/validity separation, the reported worst path is
25.068 ns across register reads, ID, EX and the ALU. Recent outcomes
repeatedly show this same 13-cell datapath, so another redirect-control
change is unlikely to remove the remaining bottleneck. EX currently
encodes a prioritized forwarding choice, decodes it into a three-way
operand mux, then selects PC or immediate through another operand mux.
Removing serial selection ahead of arithmetic can raise Fmax without
adding instruction latency or changing CoreMark's cycle schedule.
No LESSONS.md exists. The earlier micro_opt attempts targeted the old
combinational divider and redirect feedback, not this operand network.

title: Isolate multiplication in a registered shared DSP execution unit
motivation:
The champion scores 119.64 at 53.739 MHz and 4,491,817 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. The previous structural changes removed unrolled
division and redirect-to-decode feedback; the latest worst Gowin path
now crosses register-file/forwarding, EX and the combinational ALU
multiplier. The production ALU still describes three full-width
products with signed, unsigned and mixed signedness, all feeding the
ordinary result mux. Their delay constrains every instruction even
though multiplication is only a subset of CoreMark's dynamic stream.
The structural history contains no registered-multiplier attempt and
LESSONS.md is absent.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move MUL, MULH, MULHU and MULHSU out of the single-cycle integer ALU
into one clocked, shared multiply execution unit. Keep single issue,
in-order completion and the current nret=1 interface. Snapshot both
forwarded operands and the operation when EX accepts a valid multiply,
using a register boundary before the DSP logic. In the next cycle
compute and register four unsigned 16x16 partial products, denoted
ll, lh, hl and hh for the low/high operand halves. The reduction cycle
computes an 18-bit column = ll[31:16] + lh[15:0] + hl[15:0], with all
terms explicitly zero extended. MUL's result is
{column[15:0], ll[15:0]} and is marked complete immediately after this
reduction edge. In parallel, register high_base = hh + lh[31:16] +
hl[31:16] modulo 2^32 and the two-bit column[17:16] carry. A subsequent
high-half cycle registers high_base + carry, completing MULHU. Avoid a
combinational path
through operand forwarding, a full 32x32 multiplier, product reduction
and the main ALU result mux in a single clock period.

Share the unsigned product across all four operations. MUL returns
its low 32 bits, MULHU its high 32 bits; MULHSU subtracts b from the
high half when a is negative, and MULH additionally subtracts a when
b is negative, all modulo 2^32. Use one separate cycle for conditional
subtraction of b, completing MULHSU there, and another for conditional
subtraction of a, completing MULH there. This keeps each correction
stage to one 32-bit subtract and selection and avoids combining
reduction with signed correction. With a separate result-transfer
edge, low MUL adds three EX hold cycles relative to the current
single-cycle operation; do not add high-half correction latency to
low MUL. Preserve full RV32M results for negative operands, extrema
and carries from partial-product addition.

Integrate multiplication by reusing the divider's existing EX ownership
controller and snapshot register for either kind of operation:
launch only for a valid legal multiply when older data memory is not
blocking EX/MEM; capture the forwarded operands and complete RVFI
instruction metadata exactly once. Hold PC and ID/EX while multiply
owns EX, let older stages drain, and inject cleared EX/MEM bubbles
when no older memory request is held. A completed product remains
stable until EX/MEM accepts it once. Release the frontend on that
transfer, then use the existing EX/MEM and MEM/WB forwarding and
channel-0 retirement paths. Preserve outstanding memory requests,
retained MEM/WB bypass data during holds, redirect priority, load-use
handling and the iterative divider. The existing divide_wait signal
can represent either multiply or divide ownership without new hazard
or top-level logic. Dispatch the ALU's existing request/result handshake
to the selected unit from the held operation; gate each unit's request
and consumption and select its ready/valid signals consistently.
Reset cancels unfinished work.

substitutions and their single-cycle formal bypass, as with division.
Actual simulation and FPGA builds must use the registered arithmetic;

illegal and alignment traps, monotonic retirement and every fixed
evaluation contract. This is one structural change to multiply
execution, with no predictor, cache or general pipeline redesign.

motivation:

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one direction-only fetch predictor to the CURRENT iterative-divider
champion. Use 64 untagged two-bit saturating counters indexed by
PC[7:2] XOR PC[13:8], reset to weakly not taken. Predecode legal BRANCH
encodings and JAL from raw imem_data. Conditional branches predict taken
when the selected counter's MSB is set; JAL predicts taken unconditionally.
All other instructions, including JALR and reserved BRANCH encodings,
predict sequential execution. Form the direct B/J target with one shared
PC-relative immediate adder, and suppress taken prediction for a target
whose low two bits are nonzero. No target/tag table or indirect-target
predictor is needed. Predict from raw instruction data and PC independently
of recovery, hazard outputs and bus readiness; readiness controls acceptance.

Carry only a predicted_taken bit with IF and ID/EX, preserving it on
backend holds. An accepted direct taken prediction has the exact target
implied by that same instruction's latched PC and immediate, so EX need
not compare a 32-bit predicted next PC. Compute resolved_taken from the
existing legal branch/jump resolution, with target-alignment faults
treated as sequential trap behavior. On valid, advancing EX instructions,
recover only when predicted_taken XOR resolved_taken is true. Select the
existing resolved target for actual taken control flow, or PC+4 for a
falsely predicted taken branch. A correctly predicted branch or JAL
retains the younger target instruction. JALR remains unpredicted and uses
its existing forwarded target and recovery. Keep link writes and RVFI
pc_wdata based exclusively on architectural resolution.

Train exactly once per valid legal aligned conditional branch that leaves
EX; saturate the corresponding counter toward its actual outcome.
Dmem backpressure suppresses both recovery and training until advancement.
Reset clears counters; invalid bubbles, illegal encodings, JAL/JALR,
alignment traps and divider waits never train. Aliasing affects only
performance. Use small counter storage without target/tag reset or a
fetched-instruction-controlled target RAM read. Avoid write-through
table bypass; simultaneous lookup and training use the old counter.

Retain the champion's separation between payload and validity. Raw
imem_data must reach decode and register-file addresses even on recovery;
recovery kills only younger validity, without controlling wide operand
payload capture. Advance fetch along a prediction only when accepted,
excluding imem stalls, load-use bubbles, dmem holds and division ownership.
Reset has highest priority, then advancing EX recovery overrides frontend
hold and imem unavailability. A held instruction keeps its original bit.
Preserve outstanding memory requests, retained MEM/WB forwarding,
divider snapshots and exactly-once completion, both real and ALTOPS
arithmetic, trap behavior, nret=1 IO, channel-0 order and all gates.

Expect approximately 7 percent more iterations/cycle from removing warm
taken-branch and JAL bubbles. This is an estimate informed by earlier
measured predictor cycle counts, not a timing measurement for this
design. The key distinction is removing the large BTB and wide predicted
PC equality test; expect roughly preserved Fmax rather than assuming
recovery isolation will improve a path already fixed in the champion.
Fetch target-adder delay and small-counter routing remain timing risks.
At a 7 percent cycle-throughput gain, Fmax may fall by only about
2.24 percent before missing the 4.6 percent acceptance requirement.
Require unchanged formal, unit and cosim gates, canonical stalled
CoreMark CRCs, and measured median Gowin Fmax times bracketed
iterations/cycle above 125.14344 iter/sec before accepting.

implementation_notes:
# Direction-only branch prediction

Implemented the hypothesis on the current iterative-divider bench champion.

- IF has 64 untagged two-bit saturating counters indexed by PC[7:2] XOR
  PC[13:8], reset to weakly not taken. Legal conditional branches use the
  counter MSB; JAL predicts taken; JALR and reserved branch encodings remain
  sequential. B/J immediates share one direct-target adder. Misaligned direct
  targets suppress prediction.
- Added exactly one predicted_taken bit to IF and ID/EX, before instr so the
  existing low instr/valid layout stays intact. Backend holds preserve it.
  Decode and register-file addresses still receive raw imem_data on recovery.
- EX recovers on a direction XOR only when the normal instruction advances.
  Memory holds and divider ownership suppress both recovery and training.
  False-taken branches recover to PC+4; correctly predicted direct transfers
  retain the younger target instruction. Architectural pc_next and link writes
  continue using the original resolution logic and forwarded JALR target.
- Legal aligned conditional branches train once on advancement. Each entry
  updates from its own two bits using saturating Boolean equations, avoiding
  an indexed training read mux. Simultaneous fetch and training use the old
  counter; there is no bypass, target table, tag table or predicted-PC payload.
- Preserved nret=1, channel-0 RVFI/order, memory request retention, retained
  WB forwarding, divider snapshots, exactly-once completion and both real
  and ALTOPS arithmetic. No arithmetic implementation was changed.

The main implementation refinement is using is_divide/divide_active_q to
identify normal EX advancement directly. Legal branch/jump controls come
from the decoder's validated encoding arms. Training also explicitly checks
is_illegal and target alignment. Shared training predecode, sharing the fetch
adder with sequential increment, and using the prediction bit for the wide
recovery target mux were tried and reverted because measured median timing
was worse.

Retained the existing pipeline assertions, except the assertion that expected
redirect during a dmem hold: the hypothesis requires suppression until EX
advances. Its replacement verifies no held recovery/training, one recovery
and one update, while retaining the WB-forwarding and architectural checks.
Added ten directed pipeline tests covering warm-up, both saturation limits,
direction reversal, hashed collisions, old-counter lookup during simultaneous
training, consecutive warm branches, all legal branch conditions, forward
and backward JAL links, reserved encodings, alignment traps, reset,
load-dependent branches, false-taken PC+4 recovery, imem-unavailable recovery,
prolonged dmem holds and divider ownership. The harness independently models
the counters and checks raw prediction, acceptance, held metadata, inert
bubbles, memory request stability, wrong-path effects and exact RVFI order.

Local validation of the final RTL:

- Requested Verilator -Wall lint: pass, no warnings.
- pytest -v cores/bench/test/: all six suite runners pass, including 29
  pipeline tests.
- RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=8 bash formal/run_all.sh:
  **pass, 53 passed / 0 failed**. No formal failure or fix retry occurred.
- NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench: pass for selftest with and without random
  bus stalls and for stalled CoreMark CRC validation. NRET=1 is necessary
  because the direct Makefile invocation otherwise defaults the C++ harness
  to two retirement channels; no build-contract files were edited.
- NRET=1 make fpga TARGET=bench: completed, no placement/benchmark failure.
  All canonical CoreMark CRCs and "Correct operation validated." match;
  no out-of-bounds access occurred.

Measured fitness:

- Marker start/stop cycles: 15,022 / 4,205,303.
- Bracketed CoreMark cycles: **4,190,281**, 10 iterations.
- Iterations/cycle: 0.0000023864747973, a 7.1961% increase over the champion.
- Gowin placement options 0/1/2: **48.498 / 51.727 / 51.727 MHz**.
- Median Fmax: **51.727 MHz**; logic 2,885, registers 809, LUT-RAM 8.
- Fitness: **123.45 iterations/sec** (unrounded 123.4451818386).

The hypothesis does **not** meet the required 125.14344 iterations/sec
acceptance threshold. At this cycle count it needs median Fmax above
52.438617891 MHz. Cycle reduction matches the estimate, but the measured
Fmax loss is too large. The final worst path still passes through register
file/operand forwarding, the multiplier and the dmem RAM address path;
added predictor routing/placement remains a concern. Leave acceptance to
the orchestrator; this result should not be claimed as accepted.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give only ALU_MUL a single-cycle combinational fast path, retaining the
champion's registered multiplier for MULH/MULHU/MULHSU and its iterative
divider unchanged. Compute three unsigned products: ll = a[15:0]*b[15:0]
with a 32-bit result, lh = a[15:0]*b[31:16] modulo 2^16, and
hl = a[31:16]*b[15:0] modulo 2^16. Explicitly discard the upper bits of
both cross products and omit hh completely from this fast path. Signed
and unsigned low multiplication have identical modulo-2^32 results.
Use Gowin-inferred DSP products, with no fabric multiplier fallback.

Reduce x=ll[31:16], y=lh, z=hl using a 16-bit carry-save compressor:
s=x XOR y XOR z; c=((x AND y) OR (x AND z) OR (y AND z)) shifted left
one bit and truncated to 16 bits. Finish with exactly one 16-bit addition
column=s+c modulo 2^16. Return {column,ll[15:0]}. This avoids serial
three-operand carry propagation and every high-word carry/correction.
Do not truncate ll, forget shifted carry bits, or sign-normalize operands.

It advances through the existing normal_result, EX/MEM forwarding and
channel-0 retirement in the same cycle as an integer ALU instruction.

unchanged. Expose low MUL as a combinational operation in ALU unit tests;
retain every existing vector and reference result. Preserve all exact
single-cycle ALTOPS substitutions, which already model MUL combinationally.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move dependency comparison and complete ALU source-choice computation
to the cycle in which decode captures the consumer into ID/EX. Register
the selections alongside that consumer, without adding an instruction
stage. Compare incoming raw rs1/rs2 indices against the actual producers
about to enter EX/MEM and MEM/WB, rather than comparing the resident
consumer against those tags combinationally during EX. Give the upcoming
EX/MEM producer priority over upcoming MEM/WB, exclude x0 destinations,
and use real post-trap write eligibility. These tags predict where each
operand value will reside in the following EX cycle.

Export from EX the write eligibility of the bundle it will actually
transfer: a normal valid instruction after jump-alignment checks, or
the captured M-operation instruction on a completed result transfer.
Export from MEM the corresponding post-memory-alignment write eligibility
for its upcoming WB payload. Use ID/EX's destination for the upcoming
EX/MEM producer and current EX/MEM's destination for upcoming MEM/WB.
During M result transfer the held instruction and snapshot retain the
same destination. No invalid or trapping non-writer may claim bypass
priority. Derive eligibility from the actual producer logic rather than
assuming that every decoded reg_write causes a result.

Register complete one-hot ALU input selections. ALU A chooses ID/EX rs1,
EX/MEM result, WB result or the consumer PC for AUIPC. ALU B chooses
ID/EX rs2, EX/MEM result, WB result or the decoded immediate. Form the
AUIPC and immediate overrides using the validated incoming decoder
controls before the capture edge. In EX implement each data choice as
a parallel masked OR, avoiding a serial forwarded-value mux followed
by PC/immediate selection. Also register the ordinary rs1/rs2 bypass
choices used by branch/JALR, stores and RVFI operand snapshots, retaining
their existing architectural values and younger-writer priority.

including captures whose validity is killed by a redirect or load-use
bubble. Hold them on data-memory backpressure and M-operation ownership,
and initialize them on reset. A data stall retains EX/MEM and the old
WB bypass payload, so held selections remain meaningful even after
retirement validity clears. The M unit snapshots its actual selected
operands at acceptance, then uses the existing retained snapshot while
older producers drain. Its completion capture computes selections for
the newly arriving consumer against the M result entering EX/MEM.
Preserve the existing load-use bubble so a dependent load consumer
selects the completed WB load rather than its EX/MEM effective address.

file implementation/reset/write-first behavior, instruction latencies,
branch recovery, payload/valid separation, real M arithmetic and exact

motivation:
The current bench champion scores 181.41 iterations/sec at 86.601 MHz
and 4,773,836 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent.

A 64-entry registered-recovery trial passed correctness gates and

than frontend recovery. Halving direction state and lookup fanout is

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 32-entry bimodal direction predictor with a registered recovery
phase. Use untagged two-bit saturating counters indexed by
PC[6:2] XOR PC[12:8], reset weakly not taken, with constant-index local
flop updates and a four-by-eight grouped lookup of the MSB. Read
pre-edge state without training bypass. Predecode legal conditional
BRANCH funct3 and JAL from raw imem_data; predict conditional direction
from the table, aligned JAL taken and JALR sequential. Build exact
full-width B/J targets alongside PC+4 and suppress misaligned predictions.
Prediction is independent of hazard, flush and bus-ready feedback.

Carry predicted_taken and direct alignment into ID/EX. IF prepares the
direct recovery address: PC+4 for a taken prediction, direct target
otherwise. For validated B/J instructions, store that address in the
EXISTING id_ex_t.imm operand field rather than adding another 32-bit
ID/EX bank. Ordinary ALU, AUIPC, memory and JALR immediates remain exact.
Reconstruct original B/J immediates from retained instruction bits in
EX for architectural target/RVFI metadata only. JAL link remains PC+4;
JALR uses the original immediate and forwarded rs1, clears bit zero
and preserves its dynamic alignment check.

Register branch_op XOR {2'b00,predicted_taken} in ID. Use one forwarded
comparison network in EX to produce conditional direction mismatch.
Reconstruct actual outcome as mismatch XOR predicted_taken for training,
architectural pc_next and traps. An aligned conditional mismatch or
unpredicted aligned JALR creates a recovery event only on normal EX
advancement: in.valid && !stall && !is_divide && !divide_active_q &&
!recovery_valid_q. Capture its exact recovery target and a pending bit
at the edge that advances the resolving instruction into EX/MEM.
The registered pending bit and target drive fetch correction and
younger validity kills in the FOLLOWING cycle. Correct predictions
and aligned JAL retain their bubble-free path.

Treat the younger instruction captured on the mismatch edge as
speculative until that pending recovery cycle is cleared. During a
pending recovery, squash its EX/MEM capture to a completely inert
bundle, suppress upcoming producer eligibility, suppress divider and
multiplier request launch, and suppress new branch training or recovery
events. Preserve the older resolving instruction so it drains and
retires normally. A wrong-path store/load must never reach a dmem
request, and a wrong-path M operation must never acquire EX ownership.
The pending recovery flushes the subsequent fetched instruction, then
clears exactly once. This explicitly handles the extra speculative
instruction allowed by registering recovery.

Train once when a valid legal conditional branch with an aligned target
normally advances, using its reconstructed actual outcome. Older dmem
backpressure defers event capture and training; M ownership suppresses
them. Hold original prediction, alignment, complemented predicate and
reused recovery operand throughout backend holds. A resolving branch
or JALR is a non-memory instruction, so its own EX/MEM entry does not
introduce dmem backpressure during the subsequent recovery phase.
Reset clears predictor counters and pending recovery. Reset has highest
PC priority, registered recovery overrides imem unavailability next,
and otherwise PC holds or follows an actually accepted prediction.

Preserve exact taken-target alignment traps and sequential trapped
pc_next, with jump link writes suppressed on faults. Keep aggregate
trapping but qualify writing producers by applicable jump faults
rather than the non-writing conditional comparator. Maintain raw decode
payload, independent validity kills, registered complete WB results,
retained forwarding after WB valid clears, youngest-writer priority,
registered complete ALU choices, stable outstanding memory requests,
M snapshots and exactly-once results, real RV32M and ALTOPS arithmetic,
decoder default-illegal checks, nret=1 IO and monotonic channel-0 order.

The isolated 64-entry registered-recovery precursor passed warning-free
Verilator build, all 53 unchanged nret=1 ALTOPS formal checks, and full
RVFI trace cosimulation for selftest and all three random programs,
each with no stalls and both bus stalls. Canonical stalled CoreMark
completed in bounds with every required CRC and validation literal,
taking 4,527,071 marker-bracketed cycles. Gowin options 0/1/2 reached
79.755/81.429/81.429 MHz; median 81.429 MHz implies only 179.87
iterations/sec, below the champion and therefore NOT an acceptable
measured candidate. Its 4,662 logic cells and 1,889 registers include
128 counter flops; the proposed 32-entry version removes 64 of those
flops, halves local training enables, removes half the grouped lookup
and narrows the hash to five bits. Keep all recovery and speculative
squash semantics proven by that precursor.

This final 32-entry variant has not been timed or cycle-measured.
Expect roughly five percent fitness improvement if reduced predictor
routing permits about 87-89 MHz with a modest aliasing penalty. This is
a low-confidence architectural projection, not a measured gain: the
precursor's ALU critical path may remain limiting despite reduced table
size. More aliases can also increase misses, and every miss now costs
an extra registered-recovery cycle. Measure the actual bracketed cycles
and median Gowin Fmax; accept only above 189.75486 iterations/sec.
For example, 4.55 million cycles require more than 86.338 MHz. Require
all unchanged gates and explicit speculative-squash coverage on the
32-entry implementation. No evaluation or arithmetic changes are part
of this hypothesis.

title: Use synchronous mirrored block-RAM register reads at the ID/EX boundary
motivation:
The champion reaches 238.34 iterations/sec at 107.897 MHz with 4,527,071
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its resettable 31-by-32 register storage and
two combinational read trees occupy many flops, LUTs and routes. The
current ID/EX operand flops already establish a synchronous operand
boundary. Native FPGA synchronous RAM reads can implement that same
boundary while removing the wide resettable storage and decode read mux
network. LESSONS.md is absent. Prior fetch buffering and extra recovery
stages lost fitness to timing or cycle costs. Private forwarding-
qualification and JALR-interlock trials also failed vendor timing, so
neither is included. A storage/topology change offers greater structural
leverage than moving another Boolean qualifier between existing muxes.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the core's flop-based combinational register-file reads with two
mirrored 32-by-32 memories, each with one synchronous write port and one
synchronous read port. Both copies receive every architectural nonzero
register write; one supplies rs1 and the other rs2. Describe unreset data
arrays using Gowin-supported synchronous RAM inference templates, with
explicit clock enables and no vendor black boxes in the formal model.
Target two block-RAM read banks rather than distributed LUT mux trees;
confirm actual inferred resources in the vendor report.

Read addresses are the current raw decode source fields. On precisely
the existing ID/EX payload capture edge, enable both synchronous reads
and capture their zero/initialization and same-edge-WB conflict metadata.
Feed the resulting registered RAM operands directly into EX's fallback
operand inputs instead of recapturing them in ID/EX a cycle late. These
RAM read outputs are the existing operand register boundary: instruction,
PC, immediate, decoder controls, prediction metadata and bypass choices
still capture on that SAME edge. This adds neither an instruction stage
nor a dependency bubble. Hold read outputs and all associated metadata
whenever ID/EX payload holds for older dmem backpressure or M ownership.
Invalid payload captures may read normally, preserving payload/valid
separation. Keep the existing prioritized registered EX/MEM and WB
forwarding and complete parallel ALU choices, replacing only their
unforwarded regfile source. Every branch, store, M-request snapshot and
RVFI operand must use those same correct post-forward values.

Preserve architectural reset-to-zero without clearing the RAM data
arrays: reset one valid bit per architectural word, and capture a
per-read invalid/x0 indication with the read address. A word whose valid
bit is clear supplies zero. Nonzero writes set its valid bit. Reset
clears validity and all read/conflict metadata, so stale or uninitialized
RAM words never escape after cold or warm reset. x0 always reads zero
and is never written. A same-edge architectural WB write to a read
address must override the RAM's potentially unspecified read-during-
write result: register each conflict match and one shared WB data word
on the consumer's read edge, then select that captured data in EX.
The conflict override has priority over the old invalid bit, ensuring
a register's first write is immediately visible. Hold the captured
conflict data and flags with the RAM outputs during backend stalls.
Do not use live WB data or live read addresses to resolve an older read.

Integrate this synchronous interface explicitly into core/ID/EX. Remove
functionally redundant ID/EX copies of regfile data if appropriate,
while retaining full architectural RVFI source snapshots from EX. A
parameterized asynchronous compatibility implementation may preserve
existing standalone reg_file tests; the actual core must elaborate the
synchronous mirrored implementation. Avoid a combinational output mux
between synchronous and asynchronous modes. If the inferred RAM's
output clock enable cannot implement the required hold directly, use
its supported output register/enable arrangement rather than advancing
operands independently of their instruction.

Keep pipeline transfer timing, load-use bubbles, registered recovery,
direction prediction/training, exact integer and RV32M results/ALTOPS,
M ownership and completion, actual writer eligibility, retained WB
forwarding, request stability, decoder default-illegal discipline,
alignment traps, nret=1 memory/RVFI IO and consecutive retirement intact.

predictor change, speculative fault handling or extra pipeline stage.

read paths at unchanged measured cycles. The added registered WB-conflict
selection, block-RAM clock-to-output delay and EX arithmetic may become

hysteresis did not clear the timing threshold. A physically compact
direction-only memory offers a different storage implementation without
introducing wide target/tag lookup or changing the pipeline topology.

and immediately disables RAM-derived conditional predictions. Reset-time
and pre-initialization lookup must never expose unknown target control.

title: Registered circular fetch FIFO isolates decode from bus and ready feedback
motivation:
The champion scores 238.34 iterations/sec at 107.897 MHz and 4,527,071
marker-bracketed cycles. The earlier two-entry fall-through queue reduced
cycles to 4,190,068 but reached only 99.018 MHz. LESSONS.md is absent.

occupancy through decode back into fetch-PC and payload enables; even a
local one-hot three-entry shifter reached only 81.538 MHz. The strongest
remaining structural angle is a genuine registered fetch boundary with
independently written circular slots and registered producer capacity.

hypothesis.hypothesis:

existing speculative IF/predictor and ID. Every accepted fetch crosses this

one refill cycle, but removes the live imem/bus-ready-to-decode/register-

ownership holds. Keep single issue, nret=1, current execution stages,
all arithmetic and the existing predictor algorithm.

Use three constant-index 98-bit payload registers, with separate one-hot
head and tail pointers and four one-hot occupancy states. A payload
contains fetch PC, instruction, recovery address, predicted_taken and
direct_aligned; availability comes from occupancy, not a stored valid bit.
Describe each payload as a packed vector local to its generate scope,
connected by constant-index wires, rather than an unpacked struct array:
a precursor simulated correctly but that array's Yosys elaboration failed
pc_fwd. Select the head with a shallow one-hot AND/OR across three slots.
Never shift the wide payloads when decode pops an instruction.

The producer accepts only on actual io_imemReady and the registered
not-full occupancy bit, with no recovery. Only this producer acceptance
advances the fetch PC and tail pointer or enables the selected slot write.
All producer payload writes are independent of decode acceptance, load-use
comparisons, M completion and pop. When full, deliberately defer a new
fetch even if a pop happens that edge; the freed credit becomes visible
in the next registered occupancy state. Buffered instructions still drain,
so this removes combinational consumer-ready lookahead from fetch-PC and
wide payload capture. Do not reintroduce full-pop-and-replace lookahead.

Decode availability is simply registered nonempty. Pop only when this head
is available, the existing load-use/backend/M controls permit ID capture,
and there is no recovery. The pop advances the head pointer. Push alone
increments occupancy, pop alone decrements it, and simultaneous push/pop
preserve occupancy while independently advancing both pointers. Empty
decode sees invalid payload until a real fetch has been registered; the
payload may continue to capture inert data as in the champion. No raw
instruction-bus unavailability may invalidate an already buffered head.
Preserve source dependencies, x0, youngest-writer bypass priority, exact
post-trap eligibility and retained WB values during backend holds.

Keep speculative target preparation attached to raw fetch PC and word.

Reset cancels buffered and pending work. Preserve misaligned-target and

Add one focused predictor architecture: a four-entry return-address stack
paired with a two-phase JALR validation protocol. Preserve the existing
conditional direction predictor, direct JAL prediction, target preparation,
registered recovery and execution-lane reuse. Register the indirect target
before qualifying its link as a forwarding producer. Return prediction
offsets some of the added validation latency; the intended fitness gain

Implement four fixed shift-register words containing 30 aligned address
bits, a directly readable top, and a three-bit depth bounded to 0..4.
Supply target low bits 00; avoid an indexed target/tag table or wide read
mux. Update only on advancing valid legal nontrapping aligned EX/MEM
control instructions. JAL or JALR with rd=x1/x5 pushes architectural PC+4,
including indirect calls. Canonical JALR x0,x1,0 or JALR x0,x5,0 pops if
nonempty. Push/pop classes are disjoint. Shift fixed words on each update.
Overflow invalidates the stack by clearing depth and discarding that push;
underflow predicts nothing. Reset clears depth and initializes words.
Never update at speculative fetch; squashed instructions cannot change
the stack. Simultaneous lookup/update uses pre-edge state. All stack
predictions are checked against actual targets, so no checkpoint is needed.

IF predecodes canonical returns with opcode=0x67, funct3=0, rd=0,
rs1=x1/x5 and immediate=0. A nonempty stack predicts its aligned top;
other JALRs remain sequential and B/J predictions remain unchanged.
Lookup is independent of hazards, readiness and flush feedback. PC changes
only on actual fetch acceptance, with reset first and recovery overriding
holds. Carry an indirect_prediction_valid bit through IF/ID and ID/EX.
Reuse recovery_addr and ID/EX imm for the accepted stack target ONLY on
predicted canonical returns, whose architectural immediate is zero.
Hold this metadata with its instruction. Reconstruct the original signed
I-immediate from retained instruction bits for EVERY JALR calculation;
a speculative target must never become an execution offset. Preserve
original immediates and prepared alternate operands for other instructions.

Give every validated JALR one EX target-validation phase before completion.
Launch only for valid normal EX ownership, excluding pending recovery,
M ownership and older dmem holds. Snapshot actual forwarded operands and
original architectural/RVFI metadata once. Capture rs1 plus the original
I-immediate into existing effective_addr_q. Hold PC and ID/EX, insert an
inert EX/MEM bubble and let older instructions drain. Pending JALR is not
a forwarding producer. Never resample its sources after older stages move.

The next phase completes only on EX/MEM acceptance. Determine alignment
from captured target bit 1 and mask bit 0 per JALR. Qualify all JALR
link writes and next_reg_write from REGISTERED alignment and saved controls,
removing live forwarded target addition from producer eligibility.
Supply exact PC+4 through the existing arithmetic-result and bypass path.
Retire once with saved actual operands, instruction, resolved next PC,
trap status and consecutive order. Use local bounded ownership and saved
metadata; shared snapshot storage is allowed only with exclusive owners.

Retain effective_addr_q during completion, so the resolving EX/MEM JALR
owns its target until pending recovery consumes it; add no separate
recovery-target register. For a fault, suppress the link and report the
existing alignment trap with architectural next PC=PC+4. A predicted
fault must replace the owned recovery payload with PC+4 and recover there;
an unpredicted fault is already sequential. For an aligned predicted
return, compare the captured masked target with its saved stack target.
A match needs no recovery; a mismatch uses existing registered recovery
to the actual target. Other aligned JALRs retain unconditional recovery,
issued at completion. Target equality must never gate link eligibility.

Keep pending-recovery suppression of younger EX/MEM validity, memory/write
controls, forwarding eligibility, M launch/wait, secondary recovery and
stack updates. The younger instruction captured on a mismatching completion
edge cannot cause a side effect in the following pending cycle. Include
local JALR wait in frontend holds while older stages drain; preserve dmem
hold priority, stable requests, retained WB data and load-use re-evaluation
at release. Reset cancels ownership. Stack and conditional training each
occur once on valid MEM advancement, even during younger JALR/M ownership.
Preserve default-illegal decode, all alignment/reserved/SYSTEM checks,
real RV32IM and ALTOPS arithmetic, nret=1 IO and architectural RVFI.

motivation:

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Insert one two-entry circular fall-through instruction buffer between
the existing speculative IF/predictor and ID. Preserve single issue,
nret=1 and the backend pipeline. Use two constant-index 98-bit local
packed-vector payload registers holding PC, instruction, recovery
address, predicted_taken and direct_aligned. Each slot owns an
independent producer write enable. Use one-bit head and tail pointers
and three one-hot occupancy states: empty, one and full. Never shift,
copy or compact a stored payload when decode consumes an entry.
Packed vectors avoid the unpacked-struct-array formal frontend failure
documented in the r12 precursor.

When empty, decode receives the current raw fetch immediately; when
occupied, it receives the stored head. Implement this as one shallow
three-source masked OR, driven by registered mutually exclusive source
grants for raw, slot zero and slot one. Derive those grants from next
occupancy/head state on each edge and reset to raw selection. Avoid a
slot mux followed by an empty-bypass mux. Ready and consumer hazards
affect availability and transfers, never the payload-source grants.
Stored prediction metadata belongs to its accepted fetch even when
subsequent training changes predictor direction.

Producer capacity is the registered not-full state, with no full-pop
lookahead. Accept a raw fetch only on actual io_imemReady, available
capacity and no reset/recovery. This acceptance alone advances fetch
PC. When empty and decode accepts that same fetch, deliver directly
without a slot write, pointer change or occupancy change. When empty
and decode is held, store the accepted fetch in the tail slot. When
occupied and not full, write the accepted fetch into the tail regardless
of decode consumption. A full queue deliberately declines a new fetch
even when decode pops that edge; its freed credit appears next cycle.
Never reintroduce consumer-ready lookahead into fetch-PC advancement
or occupied-buffer slot writes. The empty direct-transfer decision may
suppress a slot write but cannot stall an otherwise acceptable fetch.

Consume a stored head exactly when decode can capture a valid instruction:
no load-use interlock, older dmem hold, M ownership or recovery. Stored
heads remain available when raw imemReady is zero. Feed the existing
hazard logic decode availability equal to nonempty OR actual raw ready,
separating consumer interlocks from producer hold. Stored push alone
increments occupancy, stored pop alone decrements it, and simultaneous
stored push/pop preserves occupancy while toggling both pointers. Only
stored transfers change pointers. Maintain head=tail whenever empty.
Never enqueue an unready raw word or count direct delivery twice.

Keep predictor lookup and B/J target preparation attached to raw fetch
PC and word. Buffer all metadata on producer acceptance. Train exactly
once from the advancing registered EX/MEM branch, as today. Registered
recovery overrides capacity, bus unavailability and both transfers;
clear occupancy, reset pointers/source grants and redirect PC using the
existing registered target. The resident younger ID/EX instruction still
receives the existing recovery squash before any side effect or M launch.
Reset cancels all buffered instructions.

title: Shared DSP product bank pipelines low MUL without frontend ownership
motivation: The champion scores 238.34 iter/sec at 107.897 MHz and 4,527,071 bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent; all thirteen structural experiments were reviewed. Fetch queues and synchronous register-file reads repeatedly lost frequency. Low MUL currently serializes operand snapshot, products, reduction and result transfer while holding the entire frontend. Profiling the canonical instruction stream finds 93,960 low MULs but only 35,640 immediate consumers. Pipelining low MUL through existing execution boundaries removes unnecessary global ownership, while sharing the existing product bank avoids the additional DSP and routing cost observed in a separate-lane precursor.

Reorganize the EXISTING multiplier's DSP product register bank so it serves two mutually exclusive schedules: ordinary pipelined low MUL, and the current exclusively owned MULH/MULHU/MULHSU service. Do not add a second multiplier or a duplicated EX product bank. Add an elaboration-time core-only pipelined-low-MUL option to multiplier.sv and alu.sv; their default standalone interfaces continue to provide the original blocking arithmetic and handshake behavior.

For a valid low MUL in EX, compute and register unsigned 16x16 products directly from the actual forwarded operands on the existing EX/MEM edge: ll=a[15:0]*b[15:0], lh=a[15:0]*b[31:16], hl=a[31:16]*b[15:0]. Reuse the existing ll_q/lh_q/hl_q storage and the same DSPs used by high-half multiplication; hh is irrelevant to the low result but remains available in the shared bank for high-half operations. Expose the registered low products through ALU/EX to MEM without recapturing them in another register. EX/MEM holds the low-MUL instruction metadata and ownership tag on that SAME edge. MEM computes the explicitly widened column=zero_extend(ll[31:16])+zero_extend(lh[15:0])+zero_extend(hl[15:0]); the low result is {column[15:0],ll[15:0]}, modulo 2^32. This is exact for all signed and unsigned operands. Select it before the existing MEM/WB register. Never chain DSP products and reduction in one cycle, or route reduction into the early EX/MEM bypass.

In the core's pipelined mode, a shared registered control chooses product operands: use the saved a_q/b_q when the blocking multiplier is in its registered PRODUCTS phase, otherwise use live forwarded EX operands. Low MUL cannot coexist with an owned high-half operation because the latter already holds ID/EX. Preserve the original high-half request snapshot, PRODUCTS-to-REDUCE dependency, high carry and signed correction phases, stable completed result and exactly-once result consumption. REDUCE reads the pre-edge saved products; later overwriting the product bank cannot change the already registered high_base/carry. Requests, completion, reset and transitions back to ordinary low-MUL issue must not misassociate a bank value with another instruction. In default standalone mode, retain the original PRODUCTS-only capture and full blocking MUL support.

The shared bank must hold with an outstanding older dmem request, exactly like EX/MEM. Outside that hold it may capture ordinary raw operands independently of instruction validity, bubbles and M snapshot/result muxes. Real side effects depend on a separate low-MUL tag, captured only for a valid legal advancing low MUL and cleared for invalid instructions, pending recovery, blocking M launch/busy/completion and reset. Avoid introducing request/valid/completion muxes into product data. The shared bank is the partial-product register boundary; adding another bank would repeat the measured losing precursor. Confirm Gowin reuses the champion's multiplier DSP resources instead of duplicating the low lane.

Capture an explicit validated is_low_mul bit beside the existing ID/EX execution classes, with the same reset/capture/hold behavior. A low MUL advances through ordinary EX/MEM metadata and never launches the blocking M service or asserts divide_wait. Independent younger instructions and independent consecutive MULs issue at one per cycle. MULH/MULHU/MULHSU and DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU retain current ownership, saved operands, arithmetic and backpressure. The low-MUL bit drives lane ownership and its interlock without decoding a live five-bit ALU opcode in those control paths. Outside ALTOPS, anticipated complete normal EX/MEM writers exclude the registered is_multiply OR is_divide classes directly; saved blocking-service completion keeps its separate eligibility term. Actual architectural reg_write remains true for a legal low MUL.

Treat low MUL as a late producer like a load. Extend the existing raw-source load-use comparisons to low MUL: a matching nonzero rd holds fetch and inserts a validity-only ID/EX bubble for one cycle. The retried consumer then selects the complete retained MEM/WB value. Retain raw comparisons, including unused fields, because full-RVFI cosim checks those source snapshots too; this conservative protocol also avoids validated legality decoding on the PC hold path. Preserve youngest-writer priority, x0, all memory/M holds, redirect kills and retained retired WB data. Low-MUL operands must come from the same actual forwarded values reported in RVFI. Illegal or squashed instructions cannot own a tag, advertise a writer, redirect, issue memory or launch a service.

Keep the original ALU integer/link grants and blocking-unit result lane for every other instruction. Hardware low MUL has all integer/link grants zero and no blocking completion, so its ordinary arithmetic_result_q is zero. Combine the tagged reduced low product disjointly with that lane before the existing load-versus-integer WB selection. Preserve the independent effective-address/store-data lanes, branch recovery and every alignment/trap check. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS keep all eight exact single-cycle substitutions and normal-writer eligibility, disable the real low-MUL lane/interlock, and omit its DSP expressions. Real simulation/FPGA must use the shared pipeline. Keep standalone ALU/multiplier tests and all existing checks intact.

This is one structural repartition of multiplication, with no predictor, fetch queue, shift change, cache, reorder buffer or retirement-width change. A separate-product-bank precursor passes real lint, all eight selftest/random full-RVFI cosim comparisons with/without bus stalls and all 53 unchanged fast ALTOPS formal checks. # Shared DSP product bank pipelines low MUL

Implemented the hypothesis in `cores/bench/rtl/` and extended only the allowed multiplier/pipeline tests. The core remains single issue, five stages and nret=1, with its original memory and RVFI ports.

`PIPELINED_LOW_MUL` defaults off in both `multiplier.sv` and `alu.sv`. In core mode, the existing four unsigned 16x16 expressions and `ll_q/lh_q/hl_q/hh_q` registers serve both schedules. Registered PRODUCTS state selects saved request operands; all other phases select the live raw forwarded EX sources. The bank holds on exactly the EX/MEM memory hold. PRODUCTS waits for an actual bank capture if held; REDUCE consumes pre-edge products while a subsequent capture may overwrite them. Standalone mode still captures only in PRODUCTS and retains all original blocking arithmetic latencies and handshakes.

ID/EX now captures a validated `is_low_mul` class with the other execution classes. A legal advancing hardware MUL captures only its EX/MEM ownership tag and ordinary instruction metadata alongside the shared DSP edge. No product data is recaptured at EX/MEM. MEM performs the explicitly widened 18-bit low-column sum, masks its modulo-32-bit result with the tag, combines it with the disjoint original integer/link/blocking-result lane, and selects the complete value before the existing MEM/WB register. Low MUL has zero integer/link grants and does not request or consume the blocking M service. Its architectural reg_write remains enabled, while early producer eligibility excludes the registered multiply/divide classes. High MUL and all divides retain their saved ownership/completion protocol.

The raw-source load-use interlock includes hardware low MUL and retains unused instruction-field comparisons. Immediate dependent consumers receive one validity-only bubble and then use complete retained MEM/WB data. Independent consecutive MULs advance every cycle. Recovery, invalid instructions, service launch/busy/completion and reset cannot create a low-MUL ownership tag. ALTOPS disables the real lane/interlock and preserves all eight exact substitutions and normal early writers.

Implementation detail versus the advisory layout: partial products use a separate packed wire-view port through multiplier/ALU/EX/core/MEM, instead of product fields inside the registered EX/MEM bundle. This makes the absence of a second product register bank explicit. Live product inputs use EX's existing raw forwarded rs1/rs2 values, the same values reported in RVFI, independently of the integer ALU's PC/immediate operand muxes. An initial version using full ALU operands measured 93.292/96.064/96.064 MHz; moving the live bank inputs to raw sources improved the final timing below. There is still only one shared product bank.

Tests retain all standalone arithmetic and handshake coverage. Existing pipeline architectural assertions remain intact; only assumptions about every MUL launching the blocking service were updated. Command: `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`, using the unchanged vendor flow, timed memory-side wrapper and stall generator.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| 2 | 97.667 | 12 | 2 |

title: One-hot addressed direction and weakness predictor bank
motivation:
The champion's 64-entry bimodal predictor already removes most direct
control-flow bubbles. Previous tagged target tables, RAM counters, return
validation and training-pulse feedback lost vendor Fmax. Its current read
network selects eight direction groups before a second eight-way bank mux;
direction then controls both fetch PC and the prepared recovery operand.
Simultaneously decoding both halves of the lookup index can replace that
serial selection with a parallel entry mask and balanced reduction.
LESSONS.md is absent; all predictor history entries were reviewed.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one compact bimodal predictor bank whose state is directly
represented as direction and weakness bits and whose lookup uses parallel
row/column addressing. Keep 64 entry-local two-bit states, the same exact
saturation/hysteresis policy, PC[7:2] XOR PC[13:8] hash, constant-index
training enables and pre-edge read semantics. Reset direction=0,
weakness=1. On the original training event update both bits from PRE-EDGE
state: next_direction = weakness ? train_taken : direction;
next_weakness = direction XOR train_taken. Thus strong states first weaken
on an opposite outcome, weak states reverse on an opposite outcome, and
any matching outcome strengthens. This is equivalent to the champion's
binary saturating counter, with a simpler mux/XOR update network. Keep
direction as the directly readable MSB; there is no recoding on lookup.

Split the six-bit fetch index into a three-bit row and three-bit column.
Independently decode each into eight one-hot wires using constant equality
comparisons.

For every constant entry e, form selected_direction[e] =
counter_msb[e] && row_onehot[e/8] && column_onehot[e%8]. Obtain direction
with a balanced OR reduction of those 64 terms. Both row and column
selection enter before reduction; remove the existing eight group
results followed by the case-selected bank mux. Describe the reduction
as an associative bit-vector reduction or explicit balanced four-input
tree, never a serial accumulator loop. Keep constant entry wiring and
shared row/column predecode so neither comparison is replicated 64 times.
The intended FPGA mapping combines the counter bit and the two one-hot
selectors in a LUT4, then reduces in parallel; confirm the synthesized
path actually removes the late bank-selection layer.

This is the same predictor function for every PC and every counter state:
exactly one row and column select exactly one original counter MSB.
The state encoding and parallel lookup constitute one replacement of the
bimodal direction bank; retain their exact event and instruction identity.
No lookup register, history, table-size change, native binary lookup mux,
training bypass or extra feedback cycle is included.
Preserve the original full-width B/J target adder, PC+4 increment, legal
raw predecode, target-alignment suppression, conditional direction,
unconditional aligned JAL and sequential JALR policy. Keep the wide
alternate recovery operand, ID/EX metadata, shared mismatch predicate,
registered EX recovery, execution-lane reuse and MEM training unchanged.

Preserve prediction independence from hazards and bus readiness, accepted
fetch and payload holds, recovery priority over unavailable fetch, reset,
stable memory requests, wrong-path suppression, retained WB forwarding,
exact links and architectural RVFI PCs, all alignment traps and default-
illegal decoder checks, real/ALTOPS M ownership and arithmetic, nret=1
ports and consecutive single-channel retirement. Counter updates and
predictions must match the champion cycle for cycle, including colliding
lookup/training, consecutive branches, stalls and reset cancellation.

Local segmented-target, alternate-result-grant and native-indexed-read
precursors did not clear acceptance. Direction/weakness with the original
grouped read passed the existing predictor/pipeline suites and CoreMark
cosim but reached only 105.687 MHz median. Parallel one-hot addressing
with original binary states passed the independent predictor suite and
reached 108.196/103.732/103.732 MHz across options, median 103.732.
Neither precursor improved fitness. The FINAL bank combines direction/
weakness state with simultaneous one-hot addressing and has NOT been
timed as a combined circuit; the shorter update and read dependencies
must coexist to justify this hypothesis. Do not implement either failed
precursor alone or claim their measurements apply to the final bank.
Expect six-percent fitness improvement with low confidence if its shorter
read path outweighs reduction routing and added row/column fanout. This
is a timing hypothesis, not a measured accepted improvement. Require the
existing independent counter/pipeline models, unchanged formal/cosim
gates and canonical stalled CoreMark CRCs, validation text and bounded
memory. With unchanged 4,527,071 marker-bracketed cycles, acceptance needs
median scored Gowin Fmax above 112.861528 MHz and fitness above 249.30364
iter/sec. Measure all placement options; a small placement gain is
insufficient and must not be reported as an improvement.
